title: RAW UNREVIEWED: canonical prime-denominator cells for complete rational values
summary: Modern source-only number module extending IDEA386's existing common-bar reader by one fixed choice of cells. Reduce a nonnegative rational p/q, sort the prime factors of q, and take successive remainders for all but the final numerator cell. The final quotient remains unrestricted. A complete logical frame has a unique rational readback and canonical re-encoding. This preserves the whole rational value, not historical spelling, calculation provenance or unrestricted compositional substitution of equal-valued subpieces.
origin: Root-proposed canonical completion of IDEA386, independently checked conceptually by the bounded producer. Familiar mixed-radix arithmetic and prime factorization are not claimed as new mathematics. No native data, glyph values or experimental result informed a source parameter choice.

design.mechanism: Write a complete reduced rational value through a unique ordered list of common-bar cells, using the sorted prime factorization of its denominator and a fixed mixed-radix numerator decomposition.
design.unit: One complete nonnegative rational value per logical frame; an optional message is an ordered finite list of such independently framed values. This is not a source word, sentence or unrestricted prose channel.
design.contrast: IDEA386 already gives meaningful directed evaluation of supplied cells but does not canonically choose them from a rational value. This module fixes that choice. It differs from a whole-fraction lookup table, a freely selected decomposition, and IDEA979's L/R addition path.
design.prediction: Equal complete rational values must have exactly the same logical frame; unequal values must have different frames. Prime denominators are sorted, nonfinal numerator cells are bounded remainders, and the decoded numerator/denominator are coprime. These are source-side consequences, not current native predictions.
design.scope: Complete modern number module only. No 22-working-unit carrier claim, Voynich fit, historical attestation of this canonical encoder, statistical pass, corpus encoding, decoder selection or word meaning.

input_and_preserved_information.domain: A nonnegative rational value, supplied as integers p>=0 and q>=1 in lowest terms. Zero is supplied as 0/1. Negative values and undefined fractions with denominator zero are outside this version.
input_and_preserved_information.normalization: If a caller supplies an unreduced pair, first divide both integers by their greatest common divisor. The module preserves the rational value only; original numerator/denominator wording, absolute quantity provenance and the unreduced pair are intentionally not recoverable.
input_and_preserved_information.units_and_names: No physical unit, material, person, reference, operation, polarity or sentence is silently inferred. Such information needs an external complete notation and is not supplied by this module.

writer: For denominator q=1, write the single cell (p,1). This includes the unique zero form (0,1). Do not use an empty cell list.
For q>1, factor q as b1*b2*...*bn, where every bi is prime and b1<=b2<=...<=bn. Retain repeated prime factors as separate cells. This ordering is fixed before any example or target comparison.
Set r=p. For i=1,...,n-1, set ai to the remainder r mod bi, then replace r by floor(r/bi).
Set an=r without taking another remainder. In particular, the final numerator may exceed its denominator for an improper fraction, or may be zero.
Write the ordered cells (a1,b1),...,(an,bn) in the declared logical frame. The writer has no optional spellings or selectable cell counts.
reader: Parse the complete cell frame with nonnegative integer numerators and positive integer denominators. Reject missing fields, empty lists and truncated frames.
A denominator1 is permitted only as the sole denominator of a one-cell integer frame. Otherwise require every denominator to be prime and their order nondecreasing.
For every nonfinal cell require 0<=ai<bi. The final numerator an is any nonnegative integer. Do not impose an<bn.
Starting with v=0, process the written cells from left to right using v=(v+ai)/bi. The result is the represented rational value.

For an exact canonical check, form Q=product_i bi and P=sum_i ai*product_{j<i} bj, with empty product1. Require gcd(P,Q)=1. Equivalently, reduce the value and reapply the writer, demanding the identical complete cell list.
Read each separately framed value independently. Concatenating cell lists inside one frame is a different semantic operation from putting two complete value frames next to one another.
inverse_and_uniqueness_proof: Repeated Euclidean division gives p=a1+b1*a2+...+(b1*...*b(n-1))*an. Each nonfinal remainder is unique in its range; the final quotient is also unique.
The reader recurrence gives V=sum_i ai/product_{j=i..n} bj=P/Q, so every encoded input value is recovered exactly.
For a reduced input, Q=q has a unique prime multiset, whose ascending order is unique. The division rule then uniquely fixes every ai. q=1 has its separately fixed one-cell form.

Conversely, a parsed frame satisfying the prime/order/range/coprimality checks reconstructs a reduced P/Q and is exactly the output of the writer on that value. Thus these checks characterize canonical frames, not merely value-compatible strings.

teaching_frame_not_native_binding.syntax: Use the literal teaching syntax [a1:b1,a2:b2,...,an:bn]. Every integer is written in ordinary decimal with no leading zeros, except the number0 itself. An integer is [p:1].
teaching_frame_not_native_binding.readability: Brackets delimit the complete value; a colon separates numerator and denominator; a comma separates cells. These visible punctuation marks and the decimal numerals are paid notation, not invisible structure.
teaching_frame_not_native_binding.layout: The canonical logical frame contains no whitespace. For physical writing, whitespace and line breaks are ignored by the reader, including inside a long decimal numeral; a long frame may therefore continue on following lines without changing its contents. A missing closing bracket is an incomplete frame, not a silently inferred end.
teaching_frame_not_native_binding.multiple_values: Several bracketed frames form an ordered list of values, delimited by their explicit brackets. Spaces alone do not delimit numerical fields or establish addition, multiplication or a real-world instruction.
teaching_frame_not_native_binding.limit: This is an ordinary modern teaching serialization of the cell list. It is neither a claimed historical rendering nor a proposed mapping onto the manuscript's 22 working units.

hand_checked_examples_not_computer_tests.point: The final numerator4 exceeds denominator3 legitimately. A final remainder-only rule would lose the integer part.
A zero numerator cell still contributes a denominator. Removing it changes the value.
Integers and zero are overtly represented, not empty messages.

hand_checked_examples_not_computer_tests.source_comparison: The old historical-source cells (1,5,7)/(2,6,10) have the same value but are NOT preserved by this invented normalization. Their denominator product120 and written grading are not the new denominator product24.

essential_composition_limit.old_common_bar_law: For any cell list C, define V(C) by the original common-bar reader and D(C) as the product of its denominators. Then V(X followed by C)=V(C)+V(X)/D(C). The contextual effect of C depends on BOTH V(C) and D(C).
essential_composition_limit.counterexample: B=[(1,2),(1,3)] has V(B)=1/2 and D(B)=6. Its normalized complete-value frame B'=[(1,2)] has the same V=1/2 but D=2. With X=[(1,2)], XB has value7/12, whereas XB' has value3/4. Both XB and XB' are valid canonical whole frames for those different values; the original internal suffix B need not itself be a canonical isolated-value frame.
essential_composition_limit.consequence: Equality of rational values is not a substitution congruence for arbitrary common-bar sublists. Normalize a whole isolated numerical input only. Do not replace a fragment inside a larger common-bar expression solely because it has the same standalone V.
essential_composition_limit.not_a_repair: IDEA386's original directed reader remains correct. This new normalization neither makes its fragments transparently interchangeable nor proves a general homomorphic writing channel. A full contextual module would need to preserve at least the relevant affine action, here the pair(V,D), and is not designed in this card.

effort_and_costs: Learn decimal integers, the four explicit framing/separator marks, elementary exact division and fractions, primality/factorization, and reduction by a greatest common divisor.

The writer performs denominator factorization and n-1 successive divisions. A simple hand procedure can use increasing trial divisors, retaining repeated factors; scratch arithmetic and storage are real costs.
For q>1, the cell count is the number of prime factors with multiplicity, at most floor(log2(q)); q=1 uses one cell. This is not a bound on decimal digit count or physical ink width.

Large denominators may be expensive to factor. A prime denominator gives a single literal fraction cell; the final numerator of an improper fraction may be long. No general efficiency, brevity or historical practicality claim is made.

All numerator and denominator digits, frame punctuation and optional physical whitespace are written. No whole-fraction lookup dictionary, hidden unit, source paragraph, participant or free source word is supplied.
countercases_and_scope: Nonprime denominators, an unsorted prime list, out-of-range nonfinal numerators or a reducible reconstructed P/Q may denote a number under the old reader but are noncanonical here.
For example [1:2,1:3] denotes1/2 but is noncanonical because its reconstructed3/6 is reducible; the complete-value canonical frame is [1:2].
Equivalent source fractions such as10/24 and5/12 intentionally normalize together; original calculation paths or particular subdivisions cannot be recovered from this module alone.

An arbitrary native group cannot simply be assigned a rational number and counted as explanatory success. A future manuscript test needs a separately justified numerical scope and physical realization, with a consequence not guaranteed by free value assignment.
No native symbol is declared a digit, fraction cell, bar, delimiter or quantity. There is no full-text writer, corpus statistic, scientific selection or experimental pass.

predecessor_review.source_locator: Fibonacci, Liber abbaci, Boncompagni1857, printed24-25/PDF31-32; existing owned-source collation only, no new image or scan.
predecessor_review.difference: The old sources supply the common-bar value law and examples with composite denominators. The later review explicitly leaves fixed cell choice open. Sorted prime decomposition and this canonical encoder are a modern addition, not a source-attested historical writer.

The existing Liber abbaci printed50-51 account compares calculation paths and fully reduced rational endpoints. It does not specify the present prime-ordered cell encoding. Its unresolved literal register references and old fixed arithmetic-code stops remain unchanged.

979 encodes positive proportions by L/R addition paths and reverse subtraction. This module instead uses denominator factors and radix digits and includes zero and integer cases. Both are numerical modules, not established manuscript readings.

Its mixed-radix strings allocate whole dictionary ranks and maintain a source-character counter. It is not an arithmetic value-preserving fraction encoder. No source dictionary, allocation repair or rerun is proposed.
